positions.text: Haldar, Chandra, and Franz show that semantic remote attestation can evaluate program behavior and required properties rather than a particular binary, allowing multiple implementations to pass the same checks. This supports Kaal's criteria-versus-frozen-specification distinction at mechanism level. The source is narrower: it concerns a Java TrustedVM and counterparty-specified security properties, not legal or regulatory criteria, and it does not establish that regulated technology never needs to be reopened when criteria change. Software through the trusted virtual machine also remains subject to signed-hash binary attestation.
scope_conditions: The prototype concerns Java virtual machines and remote security attestation, not sovereign local agent runtimes.
The paper tests machine-checkable security properties, not legal or regulatory criteria.
Software through the trusted virtual machine still requires signed-hash binary attestation.
The remote counterparty authors the checked policy; public authority over criteria is not addressed.
